name: Good Clinical Practice and AI
blurb: How updated GCP rules frame the use of technology in trials.
title: Good Clinical Practice and AI
answer: The ICH E6(R3) revision of Good Clinical Practice, finalised in January 2025, is built around risk proportionate trial design and data governance, which gives sponsors room to use technology including AI provided systems are fit for purpose and data integrity is protected.

reading.body:
ICH E6(R3), adopted in January 2025, permits AI in clinical trials as long as each system is fit for purpose and data integrity is protected.

The revision is built on risk proportionate trial design and data governance. That framing does not name AI as a special case. It sets a general standard for technology in trials, and AI falls under it like any other system. The practical demand is documentation: a clinical team has to record how each AI system was judged fit for purpose under its risk based quality management plan.

This matters because the constraint on AI in trials is not capability but evidence of fitness. A model that recruits patients or drafts protocol content is admissible only if the sponsor can show the judgment behind using it. That judgment lives in the quality management plan, not in the model.

The data covers one guideline revision and one implementation instruction. It does not say which AI uses have been accepted, how regulators will review specific systems, or what documentation has satisfied an inspection. It establishes the rule, not the record of compliance under it.

sections.body: Document how each AI system was judged fit for purpose under your risk based quality management plan.
